guided-v2-type: A square root of a positive integer is rational only when that integer is a perfect square.
guided-v2-builder: Check each endpoint separately and remember that only integers are allowed.
guided-v2-intersection: Keep an element only if you can find it in each set.
guided-v2-interval: Translate a strict sign into an open endpoint, and a sign with equality into a closed endpoint.
guided-v2-absolute: Since a is smaller than b, decide the sign of a minus b before removing the bars.
guided-neg-exp: A negative exponent means reciprocal, not a negative coefficient; the base must be nonzero.
guided-square-sum-check: Identify A and B, then calculate twice their product.
guided-gcf-check: Look for the largest shared integer factor and the smallest exponent of each shared variable.
guided-factor-completely: Inspect the remaining parenthesis: are both terms squares with subtraction between them?
guided-identity-method: An identity must hold for every allowed input, not just a selected example.
guided-restriction: Look at where the original denominator becomes zero, before simplifying.
guided-rational-cancel-domain: Factor both polynomials, then record the zeros of the original denominator.
guided-division: Division by a nonzero expression means multiplication by its reciprocal.
guided-lcd: Factor each denominator and keep every distinct factor with its greatest required power.
guided-compound: One common multiplier must clear every small denominator in both large parts.
guided-rational-root-domain: The square root must be real and the original denominator must be nonzero.
guided-inequality-negative: Subtract two first, then divide by a negative number.
guided-inequality-repeated: The squared factor is positive away from its zero; strict inequality excludes every zero.
guided-inequality-rational: Split the number line at the numerator zero and the denominator zero, then test signs.
guided-inequality-absolute: A distance at most five gives an AND inequality with both endpoints included.
guided-pc19-v2-distance: Use the horizontal and vertical changes as perpendicular legs.
guided-pc19-v2-write: Substitute the center into the standard form and square the radius.
guided-pc19-v2-diameter: The center is halfway between the two endpoints.
guided-pc19-v2-square: Complete one square in x and another in y.
guided-pc19-v2-normalize: Make both squared coefficients equal to one using an equivalent equation.
guided-pc19-v2-graph: Use the new center, but keep the original squared radius.
guided-pc19-v2-tangent: Distance to the horizontal axis uses the vertical coordinate.
guided-pc21-function: For each permitted input, count how many outputs are assigned.
guided-pc21-eval: Replace x by the entire input (−a) before squaring.
guided-pc21-piece: Compare −3 with the three displayed interval conditions.
guided-pc21-dq: Build both outputs before subtracting the whole second expression.
guided-pc21-domain-rule: A real even root allows a zero radicand unless another restriction excludes it.
guided-pc21-common-mistake: A function restricts outputs per input, not inputs per output.
guided-22-family: Read the horizontal and vertical shifts in absolute-value vertex form.
guided-22-piece: Equality decides which interval contains the boundary.
guided-22-abs: Locate where the expression inside the absolute value changes sign.
guided-22-grapheq: Use y=a∣x−h∣+k and substitute the vertex coordinates.
guided-22-floor1: Choose the greatest integer not exceeding negative seven tenths.
guided-22-vlt: The vertical line fixes one input and tests how many outputs it has.
guided-22-equation: Isolate y and count its outputs for a chosen x.
guided-23-first: Domain records which inputs are represented.
guided-23-end: Parentheses exclude an endpoint; brackets include it.
guided-23-change: Net change is final output minus initial output.
guided-23-compare: An equation in x is solved by the horizontal coordinate of a crossing.
guided-23-inc: Follow the curve as input increases, regardless of the sign of the output.
guided-23-max: Distinguish the input location, the point, and the output value.
guided-26-shift: Inside operations act inversely on the input; outside operations act directly on the output.
guided-26-map: Solve 2(X−4)=1 for the new input, then transform the output.
guided-26-rule: For a left shift, the inside input reaches each old value sooner.
guided-26-even: Compute f(−x) and prove equality with f(x) or −f(x).
guided-numerical: Compare 5.9,5.99 with 6.1,6.01. Which output do both groups get closer to?
guided-graphical: Cover the filled point. Trace the nearby curve toward x=2 from both sides and read the height.
guided-one-sided: The minus sign means inputs less than 1. Follow only the branch to the left of the target.
guided-value: Read two things separately: the filled point for f(2), and both nearby branches for the limit.
guided-dne-jump: A two-sided limit must agree with both one-sided limits. Compare 2 and 5; do not average them.
l13-guided-diagnose: Distinguish an indeterminate form from a value or a conclusion.
l13-guided-substitution: Square −2 first, then handle the sign in −4(−2).
l13-guided-factoring: Recognize x2−9 as a difference of squares.
l13-guided-synthetic: Include the missing x2 coefficient: divide coefficients 1,0,−7,−6 by x−3.
l13-guided-fractions: Combine the numerator as (2−x)/(2x) and use 2−x=−(x−2).
l13-guided-conjugate: Keep both terms unchanged and reverse only the sign between them.
l13-guided-fractional-substitution: Use a common multiple of the denominators 3 and 2.
l13-guided-piecewise: Use x+1 on the left and 5−x on the right; let x approach 2 in each.
l13-guided-floor: Just below −2, the inside is just below 1; just above −2, it is just above 1.
l13-guided-oscillation: Distinguish an unbounded inside expression from the bounded sine output.
l13-guided-composite: The condition concerns the outer function at the inner limiting value.
l13-guided-trig: Match the denominator to the angle 5x, then compensate with a constant.
l13-guided-identity: Use 1−cos(2x)=2sin2x before applying a special limit.
l13-guided-difference: Expand the square, subtract x2, then divide every remaining term by h.
l13-guided-squeeze: Evaluate the limits of the two bounding functions, not just their signs.
continuity-point: Test the value, the two-sided limit, and whether they agree.
continuity-predict-0: Cancel the common factor only for nearby inputs.
continuity-discontinuity: Compare the two finite one-sided limits.
continuity-families: Solve the denominator equation before deciding the domain.
continuity-predict-1: Substitute the breaking input into each rule.
continuity-piecewise: Evaluate each rule on its own side of the break.
continuity-predict-2: Evaluate both pieces at their shared boundary.
continuity-predict-3: Near zero, the product is −x on the left and 0 on the right.
continuity-special: Just below an integer, the floor is the preceding integer.
continuity-closed: At the left endpoint, approach through points inside the interval.
continuity-predict-4: Check continuity and the signs of the endpoint outputs.
continuity-ivt: Separate the hypotheses from the existence conclusion.
continuity-predict-5: Compare the negative value at one with the positive value at one and a half.
continuity-bisection: First check whether the midpoint itself is a zero; otherwise retain opposite signs.
guided-15-direction: Check the sign of the denominator separately on each side.
guided-15-check-graph: Compare the two sides; do not average infinity.
guided-15-candidates: Factor x2−9 and evaluate the numerator at each zero.
guided-15-check-factor: Check the reduced denominator at the excluded value.
guided-15-check-power: Test an even power at small positive and negative inputs.
guided-15-check-trig: Rewrite tangent as sine divided by cosine.
guided-15-property: From the left, sinx→1 and cosx→0+.
guided-15-sketch: Separate input direction (left/right) from output direction (up/down).
c21-guided-slope: Identify the change in output and divide by the nonzero change in input.
c21-guided-secant: Think of the horizontal distance between the two approaching inputs.
c21-guided-definition: Replace the entire input x by x+h before expanding.
c21-guided-cancel: Every term in the numerator contains a common factor h.
c21-guided-tangent: Find both f(2) and f′(2); one supplies the point, the other the slope.
c21-guided-rate: Position has units of distance; its time derivative has units of distance per time.
c21-guided-domain: A derivative can only be taken at an input where the original function is defined in the required neighborhood.
c223-predict-terms: A constant does not change as the input changes.
c223-guided-power: Multiply by the old exponent, then reduce that exponent by one.
c223-predict-rewrite: Combine the real square-root restriction with the nonzero denominator.
c223-guided-rewrite: A reciprocal power can be written with a negative exponent.
c223-guided-trig: The derivative of cosine contributes a negative sign.
c223-predict-product: Label the original factors before taking their derivatives.
c223-guided-product: Differentiate one factor at a time while keeping the other factor unchanged.
c223-predict-quotient: The Quotient Rule squares the original denominator.
c223-guided-quotient: Keep denominator times derivative of numerator first, then subtract the other product.
c223-predict-motion: First velocity is linear in time; its derivative is its constant slope.
c223-guided-higher: Follow position to its first time derivative, then differentiate once more.
c223-guided-speed: Speed is the magnitude of velocity, not acceleration.
chainChecks-identify: Name the complete expression receiving the outermost operation.
chainChecks-order: Differentiate each layer and multiply their derivatives.
chainChecks-power: Differentiate the whole inside polynomial separately.
chainChecks-trig: Sine changes to cosine; the inner derivative supplies another factor.
chainChecks-mixed: Apply Product Rule to the whole expression and Chain Rule inside the sine factor.
implicitChecks-y: The input of the fourth power is itself the function y(x).
implicitChecks-collect: Treat dy/dx as the common unknown to isolate.
implicitChecks-product: Both x and y(x) are changing factors.
implicitChecks-trig: Differentiate sine while retaining its input, then differentiate that input.
implicitChecks-slope: Differentiate first to get 2x+2ydy/dx=0, then use the point.
ratesChecks-time: Differentiate the outer power, then multiply by the rate of its inside.
ratesChecks-sign: Identify the changing quantity and whether it increases or decreases.
ratesChecks-substitute: Instantaneous values describe one instant, not constants for all time.
ratesChecks-ladder: Use dy/dt=−(x/y)dx/dt and the signed horizontal rate.
ratesChecks-cone: Differentiate the similarity relation with respect to the same time variable.
ratesChecks-shadow: Write the total distance from the pole to the tip before differentiating.
c1-transfer-local: Check the two-sided limit first, then compare it with the actual value.
c2-transfer-definition: Subtract the output at the target from the output at the nearby input.
p1-guided-point: Substitute the x-coordinate and compare the output with the proposed y-coordinate.
p1-predict-intercepts: Factor out x, then use the difference of squares.
p1-guided-intercept: Points on the vertical axis have zero horizontal coordinate.
p1-guided-symmetry: Replace both x and y by their negatives and simplify.
p1-predict-intersections: At a common point, both formulas give the same output.
p1-guided-intersection: An intersection is an ordered pair satisfying both equations.
p1-guided-model: At an intercept on the horizontal time axis, the volume equals zero.
p3-guided-relation: Inspect repeated inputs, not repeated outputs.
p3-guided-evaluate: Put parentheses around the negative input before squaring.
p3-guided-domain: Require the radicand to be nonnegative for a real square root.
p3-predict-composition: Apply g first, then feed its entire output into f.
p3-guided-composite-domain: The output of the inner function must be allowed as the input of the outer function.
p3-guided-evenodd: Compute f(−x) and compare it algebraically with f(x) and −f(x).
p3-guided-absolute: Choose the condition first: is 0 less than 1?
pw-guided-continuity: Compare the actual value with both one-sided limits.
pw-guided-slopes: One derivative at the join must give the same finite slope from either direction.
pw-guided-stop: Check the left limit and the value at zero before comparing formulas.
pw-guided-parameters: Use both equations: a+b=2 for continuity and a=2 for matching slopes.
pw-guided-corner: There must be one shared slope; do not combine different slopes arithmetically.
